The diffraction profiles of five representative specimens (Cast-SS, ACR, ACR-650, ACR-850, and ACR-950) consistently revealed three dominant phases: FCC γ-matrix, L12-type ordered precipitates, and B2-structured intermetallic compounds.
The as-cast FCC matrix displays equiaxed grains with an average size of ~125.6 μm, containing BCC-structured secondary phase precipitates (~1.6 %) preferentially segregated at grain boundaries.
The back-scattered electron (BSE) image of the Cast-SS specimen exhibited a typical columnar dendritic morphology with pronounced micro segregation of trace Ti element at the interdendritic regions.

In contrast, the ACR specimen (Fig. 1b2) demonstrated intensive shear band formation, resulting in improved elemental homogeneity.

STEM analysis further revealed nanoscale structural features, including shear bands, dislocation tangles, coherent L12 nanoprecipitates, and homogeneous elemental distribution within a localized region

Following ACR processing, the microstructure undergoes substantial refinement, exhibiting pronounced elongation along the rolling direction (RD) with an average grain size reduction to ~4.1 μm as determined by crystal misorientation analysis of high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs, > 10°).
Notably, the ACR-processed microstructure contains 86.5 % LAGBs, indicating predominant dislocation-mediated deformation.
Notably, annealing twins with characteristic straight boundaries become prevalent at 850~950 °C.

The EDS point analysis quantitatively confirms the secondary phase composition as Al of ~16.3 at. %, Ti of ~10.7 at. %, and Ni of ~37.4 at. %, consistent with γ'-Ni3(Al, Ti) phase formation predicted by Thermo-Calc simulations in Fig. 1d
